subject.title: fix(cli): reject oversized --file input before reading in config patch

question: Should the documented `config patch` command gain a new hard input limit and regular-file-only policy, and if so what canonical limit and input modes should it cover?
rationale: The repository has no existing config-patch size contract to move earlier, so choosing 1 MiB changes valid upgrade behavior and cannot be resolved as a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Preserve current contract
options.body: Do not add the 1 MiB rejection in this PR; retain unrestricted documented JSON5 patch input until a concrete product limit is justified.

options.title: Define a canonical limit
options.body: Approve and document a shared limit for file and stdin inputs, then implement a bounded reader with fresh-install and upgrade coverage.

options.title: Pause this hardening
options.body: Close or pause the PR if local operator-selected files are not considered a sufficiently important resource boundary to justify a breaking CLI constraint.

recommendation.title: Preserve current contract
recommendation.body: Do not add the 1 MiB rejection in this PR; retain unrestricted documented JSON5 patch input until a concrete product limit is justified.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal connects this person to the central config CLI implementation and broader CLI contract refactors.
